events.desc:
During the Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Mahotsav, Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a ‘kol’ to take all to Akshardham. This was to be the final time he gave such an ‘Akshardhamno kol’. 

All were witness to his unparalleled ishta-bhakti on this occasion as well. In every moment of his life, he put God forward. Age, circumstances, the scale of his achievements over all these decades, even the condition of his own body could massively change, but nothing could sway him from his ishta-bhakti. That remained unchanging, because that is who he was, at his core. The same ishta-bhakti he had throughout his life, was the same ishta-bhakti he had in the final year of his life, when his hands could barely move, but he'd still always reach out for his beloved Thakorji, because that devotion to God was never something he learnt or cultivated; it was who he was.

For many around the world, this ‘Akshardhamno kol’ is etched in their hearts as a permanent reminder of the everlasting and eternal peace that the Satpurush can grant. Despite the many challenges, hardships, and miseries life can bring, in such moments, the Satpurush can grant us with bliss. Such reassurances fill hearts with joy and security and make so many fearless in the face of death, disease, disappointment and despair.

Last diksha given by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, as part of Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Utsav.

After a lifetime of inspiring hundreds of youths on the path of tyagashram and many joyous, divine diksha mahotsavs, this would be the final time that Swamishri gave tyagi diksha.

From 1971 to 2016, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ordained more than 1000 youths as sadhus. To inspire this many individuals from around the world, at the prime of their life, to give up their personal ambitions, to overcome worldly desires, and dedicate their entire lives to serving society, guru and God is nothing short of a miracle. A miracle stemming from the selfless love, purity, deep spirituality, and godliness of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. 

Alongside inspiring such youths, he inspired parents to happily grant permission for their children to become sadhus. Witness the moving story of one such couple whose son took diksha on that very day: https://youtu.be/Y1WjiRIeTA4?t=3190.

On the auspicious day of Jaljhilani Ekadashi on 2 September 2017, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha ceremony of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Murti. He also inaugurated the artistically mesmeric Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Mandapam at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

The Abhishek Mandapam houses the sacred image of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, the childhood form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. At the age of four, Ghanshyam climbed a pipal tree and looked westwards. When friends asked where he was looking, Ghanshyam replied, “Towards the spiritual aspirants in the West.” 

Ghanshyam was later known as Nilkanth Varni throughout his extensive travels across the length and breadth of India for seven years. He eventually settled in the western state of Gujarat and established the Swaminarayan Sampradaya which continues with a spiritual lineage of gurus to guide aspirants on the spiritual path.

The abhishek mandapam was specially designed to depict the incident from Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s childhood and features a murti of Ghanshyam climbing the pipal tree.

Following the vedic pratishtha rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj offered the first abhishek to Ghanshyam Maharaj with the waters of 108 holy rivers from India.

With Hindu rites and amidst Vedic chants, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the stambh pujan ceremony over four sessions. Countless volunteer-hours and many prayers for the installation of the first marble pillar of Swaminarayan Akshardham culminated into this auspicious moment.

Mahant Swami Maharaj met with former President Barack Obama in Washington D.C. 

Mahant Swami Maharaj presented President Obama with a garland as part of a traditional Hindu greeting as well as an Amrut Kalash. Mahant Swami Maharaj also gifted President Obama a sanctified mala and a copy of the book Transcendence.

Mahant Swami Maharaj took time to specifically praise President Obama when he learned that President Obama had set aside time, even as President, to have dinner with his family five nights a week.

Mahant Swami Maharaj was also touched by President Obama’s humility, sharing with the President a verse from a John Bunyan poem, “He that is down, need fear no fall. He that is low, no pride. He that is humble ever shall have God to be his guide.”  

As Mahant Swami Maharaj was departing, President Obama respectfully bid him farewell with the greeting: “Jay Swaminarayan.”

2 September 2017

On the auspicious day of Jal-Jhilani Ekadashi on 2 September 2017, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha ceremony of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Murti. He also inaugurated the artistically mesmeric Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Mandapam at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

The Abhishek Mandapam houses the sacred image of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, the childhood form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. At the age of four, Ghanshyam climbed a pipal tree and looked westwards. When friends asked where he was looking, Ghanshyam replied, “Towards the spiritual aspirants in the West.” 

Ghanshyam was later known as Nilkanth Varni throughout his extensive travels across the length and breadth of India for seven years. He eventually settled in the western state of Gujarat and established the Swaminarayan Sampradaya which continues with a spiritual lineage of gurus to guide aspirants on the spiritual path.

The abhishek mandapam was specially designed to depict the incident from Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s childhood and features a murti of Ghanshyam climbing the pipal tree.

Following the Vedic pratishtha rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj offered the first abhishek to Ghanshyam Maharaj with the waters of 108 holy rivers from India.

---

2 February 2026
Atladra, India

Mahant Swami Maharaj receives Guinness World Records certificate recognising the largest simultaneous Hindu text recital. 

The recognition followed a year-long effort in which 15,666 children worldwide aged between three and 13 years completed the full Sanskrit mukhpath with recitation of the Satsang Diksha, a scripture composed by Mahant Swami Maharaj comprising 315 shlokas that offer guidance for spiritual, moral, social and practical living.

Guinness World Records officials confirmed that 12,723 children were physically present at the venue and were formally counted for the record.

The certificate was officially presented to Mahant Swami Maharaj at the Janma Jayanti Celebrations on 2 February 2025.
